newsitem.title: JORDAN: Anadarko to drill first Jordan well in Sep.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko to drill first Jordan well in Sep.

text.p: U.S. Anadarko Petroleum Corp said on Friday it hoped to begin its first test drilling in the northeastern basalt plateau region of Jordan in September.
"We are hoping to start drilling our first well some time in September," said John Edge, vice president, resident manager of Anadarko's wholly-owned operations in Jordan.

The first well lies in the northern portion of a 4.2 million acre concession, known as the Safawi Bloc, which Anadarko was awarded under a 25 year production-sharing accord signed with Jordan in March 1996.

Anadarko is committed under the accord to invest at least $20 million of which a minimum $5 million are allocated for the first exploration phase which covers two and half years of a total eight and half years.
But Edge told Reuters that Anadarko will "probably by far exceed the minimum expenditure" stipulated in the agreement.
Anadarko this week also signed a services agreement with state-owned National Petroleum Company (NPC) to act as drilling contractor for the rest of the year, Edge said.
Under the several million dollar contract, NPC will provide the drilling crew and rigs.
The company's 1997 work plan focuses on drilling two startigraphic test wells to confirm the existence of a working petroleum system, Edge said.

"Once we establish a petroleum system, we will go on from there to explore in a more traditional way, with seismic work," said Edge. Activities since starting operations earlier this year had focused on geological work.

Asked about the oil potential in the concession, Edge said: "We are very excited about the hydrocarbon potential of Jordan. If we were not excited we would not be here...We are planning for long-term success."

A number of U.S. companies over the last two years have shown renewed interest in exploring for oil and gas in Jordan. Foreign firms left in the 1980s after unsuccessful drilling costing millions of dollars.

Officials say TransGlobe is also preparing to develop a concession it won last year to drill wells in the Dead Sea area while Amoco is studying the feasibility of a pipeline to bring Egyptian gas to Jordan.
